newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas mostly ends up on weather, technicals.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas mostly ends up on weather, technicals.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures mostly ended higher Friday in moderate trade, boosted by forecasts for colder Midwest weather next week and more technical buying and short covering, industry sources said.
February rallied 21.6 cents to close at $3.106 per million British thermal units. March settled 17.1 cents higher at $2.794. Most others ended up by 0.1 to 11.1 cents.

"The market has retraced about 50 percent of what it lost, but there's still plenty of gas out there, and the screen may be getting a little ahead of itself," said one East Coast trader, referring to Hub cash in the $2.55-2.60 area.

Traders said Thursday's AGA data showing a robust 128 bcf weekly gas stock draw also helped fuel some buying. But the report also showed Consuming region East stocks stood about 13 percent above last year.
The National Weather Service 6-10 day forecast calls for mostly below-normal temperatures in the Midwest and Texas, with the East likely to range from normal to above-normal.
Technically, traders now pegged February resistance in the $3.30-3.40 area, with further selling likely at the $3.595-3.61 gap and then at the contract high of $4.02. Support was seen around $2.60.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices were talked up slightly Friday to the mid-$2.50s. Midcontinent prices were five to 10 cents higher in the mid-$2.30s. New York city gate gas was little changed at about the $3.50 level.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip gained 5.7 cents to $2.413.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas futures did not trade Thursday.

On the KCBT, February closed up 19 cents at $2.90, while deferreds finished three to 14 cents higher. The East/West spread widened by 2.6 cents to 20.6 cents (NYMEX premium). ((J Silha, New York Power Desk 212-859-1624))
